tests.description: The two default haptics are qualitatively distinct, pinning the must-feel-different guarantee.
A fresh store is right-handed, silent, and carries the distinct default haptic pairing of increment Rigid and decrement Soft.
A legacy single hapticOption value seeds both new direction haptics when the new per-direction keys are absent.
A legacy hapticOption of off migrates to both directions off rather than the new Rigid or Soft defaults.
A present per-direction haptic key wins over the legacy hapticOption key for that direction.
SoundOption and HapticOption allCases cover the picker choice sets and labels
changing one option does not disturb the other settings
changed settings persist across a store reload
reads seeded string-injected preferences including option enum rawValues
A distribution-policy launch over an unstamped container ignores seeded and legacy haptic keys and starts from the Rigid and Soft defaults.

HapticOption.resolve migrates removed amplitude/rigid rawValues to their nearest surviving feel (rigid/heavy/medium to sharp, light to soft), passes current cases through, and returns nil for unknown or nil tokens.
An unrecognized or missing haptic or sound value falls back to that direction's built-in default.
Every override pinned at once still reads hasFeedbackOverride true.
A blank slot with no overrides leaves hasFeedbackOverride false.
A decrement-haptic override alone makes hasFeedbackOverride true.
An explicit off sound override is a deliberate pin, so hasFeedbackOverride is true.
A handedness override alone makes hasFeedbackOverride true.
An increment-haptic override alone makes hasFeedbackOverride true.
A counter on pure app-wide defaults pins nothing, so hasFeedbackOverride is false.
A sound override alone makes hasFeedbackOverride true.
Every distinct feel (soft, sharp, double, buzz) gates as non-off, so each fires the haptic emitter once carrying its own choice.
neither flag fires nothing
both flags on fires both emitters once each
haptic flag on and sound off fires only the haptic emitter
NoopCounterFeedback changed is a safe silent no-op for any flags
sound flag on and haptic off fires only the sound emitter
Consecutive addCounter calls stack multiple blank slots each with a distinct id
addCounter appends a blank slot with empty name blank color and count zero and selects it
addCounter assigns an id and order one past the current maximums
Adding a counter clears any pending reset-undo
addCounter persists the grown counters list and new selection across a reload
A blanked slot stays selectable and increments into a solid blank dot without resurrecting a name — incrementing does not clear blankness.
A negative excursion pulls the chart's plotted domain below zero and places the zero line between the extremes.
The chart's pure point mapping spans the plot rect and returns the data-derived count and time domain.
A clamped subtract that changes the count records the actual applied delta, not the full step.
The cumulative-series helper reconstructs the running count over relative time starting from the origin.
the default effectiveFeedback resolves to off/off options
Deleting a counter past the four permanent base slots removes it outright and selects the previous counter, instead of blanking it in place.
Deleting a counter blanks it in place: the row length is unchanged, the id is still present, its name is empty (isBlank), count is reset to 0, and it stays selected.
Deleting a counter clears its recorded histories so a blank slot starts clean.
Deleting the last counter blanks it in place: the row length is unchanged and the blanked slot stays selected, with no selection clamp.
Deleting a counter clears the pending undo.
Deleting every one of the four base slots blanks them all in place, so the counter row never shrinks below baseSlotCount.
Removing an extra counter drops its recorded runs rather than orphaning them under an id that is no longer present.
Deleting the last extra counter selects the new last counter, leaving selection in range.
Deleting an extra counter that is not last closes the gap: the counter after it slides down into its position and selection lands on the counter before it.
Editing the active counter invalidates the captured pre-reset value.
With no override set every effective resolver returns the supplied app default unchanged.
A set override pins its own value regardless of the app default, including an explicit off winning over a non-off default.
Fresh model with no seed falls back to four starter counters at zero with the first selected
A per-counter handedness override drives the effective bottom-bar layout independent of the app default.
A counter can pin one haptic direction while the other follows the app default.
Recorded runs persist and reload through the same UserDefaults suite.
The per-counter run list caps at 10, dropping the oldest run when an 11th would open.
Incrementing the counter clears the pending undo.
Incrementing fires the resolved increment haptic rather than the decrement one.
A counter with step 5 increments in jumps of 5.
Increment raises only the active counter by one
Increment appends a positive event of the counter's step to the current run, lazily opening the first run.
Feedback fired on increment resolves through the active counters override, its pinned sound and haptic winning over the app defaults.
Counters persisted before the step field existed decode with step defaulting to 1.
Legacy persisted counters written before the override fields decode with all three overrides nil.
A counter persisted with the legacy single hapticOverride migrates that value into both direction overrides on decode.
Loads seeded counters and selected id injected via UserDefaults
Legacy migration folds a persisted deletedDefaultIds set into blank counters at the correct orders on load.
Giving a blank slot a name via settings revives it — it stops being blank.
A new per-direction override key in persisted JSON wins over a legacy single override present alongside it.
The no-op subtract clamp records no event and opens no history.
A nil-override counter tracks a changed app default while an overriding counter stays pinned.
The relative-offset helper measures seconds from the run's start to an event.
The relative-time formatter renders mm:ss, escalating to h:mm:ss past an hour.
A distribution-policy AppSettings launch over an unstamped container ignores injected sound, haptic, and handedness keys and uses built-in defaults.
A distribution-policy launch ignores injected counter state lacking the provenance marker and falls back to the four default starter counters.
Once provenance is stamped, a distribution-policy AppSettings launch trusts the containers own settings again.
Under the distribution policy a real users own data survives: after the app persists and stamps provenance, a reload trusts it.
reset and undoReset are not count changes and fire no feedback
Resetting a counter already at zero still enters undo mode; undoing restores zero as a harmless no-op.
Reset captures the pre-reset value and enters undo mode: count is zero and canUndoReset is true for the active counter.
Reset seals the current run and opens a new empty run while zeroing the count.
Reset zeroes the active counter without touching the others
A hand-authored counterHistories JSON seed loads with correct deltas and relative offsets.
The seed read coerces a string-injected value via integer(forKey:).
A model seeded with the resetUndo key enters undo mode on launch when the active counter is at zero.
A seeded resetUndo key is ignored when the active count is non-zero, so a stale leftover key cannot falsely activate undo.
A scenario that seeds a subset of counters with no deletedDefaultIds exposes no blank slots — absence of a default id no longer sprouts a slot.
Selecting next within the list advances by one and does not grow the list
Selecting next past the last counter appends a fresh blank slot and selects it instead of wrapping
Select-previous within the list moves back by one
Select-previous wraps from the first counter to the last and never grows the list
With negatives disallowed, a step that would overshoot below zero clamps to zero rather than skipping the change.
Subtract clamps at zero when allowNegative is false
Subtracting clears the pending undo.
Subtracting fires the resolved decrement haptic, distinct from the increment default under the Rigid or Soft pairing.
Subtract goes below zero when allowNegative defaults to true
Subtracting honors the step symmetrically when negatives are allowed.
the no-op subtract clamp fires no feedback
Subtract records the actual negative applied delta.
Switching counters expires the undo offer and it does not revive on returning.
The debug trust policy still adopts injected seeded counters, so codeyam captures keep seeding the app.
undoReset restores the count and pops the empty run so the sealed run is active again.
undoReset restores the captured value and exits undo mode.
An unrecognized override rawValue in seeded JSON decodes to nil rather than crashing the whole load.
A step value below 1 is clamped up to 1.
Saving with nil overrides clears any previously pinned override values.
updateActiveCounter applies every edited field and persists across a reload.
updateActiveCounter persists all three overrides across a reload with enum overrides surviving as their rawValue.
Exhaustive invariant: from every starting combination, neither toggle can leave both settings panels open at once.
Nothing is open out of the box: a default SettingsOverlays has neither settings panel showing.
The core exclusivity rule: opening App Settings while the per-counter panel is up force-closes the per-counter panel.
Opening App Settings from a clean screen just opens it, leaving the per-counter panel closed.
The exclusivity rule in the other direction: opening the per-counter panel force-closes App Settings.
Opening the per-counter panel from a clean screen just opens it, leaving App Settings closed.
Toggling an already-open App Settings closes it and does not open the per-counter panel in its place.
Toggling an already-open per-counter panel closes it and does not open App Settings in its place.
Unknown colorKey falls back to the lime accent hex
Each known colorKey maps to its design-token hex
Hex parsing is case-insensitive
Each isolated color channel maps to the expected fraction of 255
Lime accent hex decomposes into its three channels
Black and white hex parse to the range endpoints
A leading hash is tolerated and parses identically
The "must feel different" guarantee, pinned: the two default haptics are qualitatively distinct, not the same tap.
A fresh store with nothing seeded is right-handed, silent, and carries the distinct default haptic pairing: increment Sharp, decrement Soft.

Legacy migration: a user who tuned the pre-split single hapticOption key (and has neither new key) adopts that value for BOTH directions. A stored amplitude value (heavy) migrates to its nearest surviving feel (sharp).
A legacy "off" is respected — both directions stay silent, not reset to the new Sharp/Soft defaults.
A new per-direction key wins over the legacy key when both are present. The legacy amplitude value (heavy) still migrates to sharp.
The option enums expose the full choice sets the settings picker renders.
Each key is independent — changing one does not disturb the others.
Changing a setting persists it: a second store over the same backing reads the written values back.
The store reads seeded preferences, including the string-injected form the seeder writes (enum rawValue via string), including the soft/sharp values.
A release-policy launch over an unstamped store ignores injected keys (including the legacy key) and starts from the Sharp/Soft defaults.
resolve(...) migrates removed amplitude/rigid rawValues to their nearest surviving feel, passes current cases through, and rejects unknown tokens.
An unrecognized option rawValue falls back to the built-in default; a missing haptic key likewise falls back (to its direction's default).
Every add stacks another blank slot, each with its own unique id.
addCounter appends a blank slot (empty name, blank color, count 0) and selects it.
addCounter assigns an id one past the current max and an order one past the max.
Adding a counter is a fresh start, so it clears any pending reset-undo.
addCounter persists both the grown counters list and the new selection.
A blanked slot increments into a solid blank dot without resurrecting a name.
A clamped subtract that DOES change the count records the actual applied delta.
The cumulative-series helper reconstructs the running count over relative time, starting from (0, 0); runningTotal is the net.
The default (no effectiveFeedback set) resolves to all-off and fires OFF options.
Past the four permanent base slots, deleting removes the counter outright and selection falls back to the previous counter.
Deleting a counter blanks it in place rather than removing it.
Deleting a counter clears its recorded runs — a blank slot starts clean.
Deleting the last counter blanks it in place: the row length is unchanged and the blanked slot stays selected.
Deleting a counter clears the pending undo.
The blank-in-place / remove split is keyed on baseSlotCount, so the row can never shrink below it no matter how many base slots are deleted.
Removing an extra counter drops its recorded runs rather than orphaning them.
Deleting the last extra counter selects the new last counter.
Deleting an extra counter that is not the last one closes the gap.
Editing the active counter invalidates the captured pre-reset value.
With no override set, every effective* resolver returns the supplied app default.
A set override pins its own value regardless of the app default — including an explicit OFF winning over a non-OFF default; the two haptic directions resolve independently.
A fresh model with no seeded state falls back to the four-counter starter set, all at zero, with the first counter selected.
A per-counter handedness override drives the effective layout independent of the app default.
A counter can pin one haptic direction while the other follows the app default.
Recorded runs persist and reload through the same store.
The per-counter run list caps at 10, dropping the oldest once an 11th run opens.
Incrementing — the counter "starting again" — clears the pending undo.
Incrementing emits one feedback call carrying the resolved sound and the increment haptic (not the decrement one).
A counter with step 5 increments in jumps of 5 (0 -> 5 -> 10).
Incrementing raises only the active counter's count by one.
Increment appends a positive event (of the counter's step) to the current run, lazily opening the first run on the first change.
Feedback fired on increment resolves through the active counter's override.
Counters persisted before step existed decode with step defaulting to 1.
Legacy persisted counters decode with all overrides null.
A counter persisted with the pre-split single hapticOverride key migrates that value into BOTH direction overrides on decode; heavy migrates to sharp.
The model loads seeded counters and the selected id injected via the store.
Legacy migration: deletedDefaultIds folds blank counters at the right orders.
Giving a blank slot a name via settings revives it — it stops being blank.
A new per-direction override key in persisted JSON wins over a legacy single key.
The no-op subtract clamp records no event — and opens no history at all.
A nil-override counter tracks a changed app default; an overriding counter is pinned.
The relative-offset helper measures seconds from the run's start.
AppSettings applies the same gate: a release-policy launch over an unstamped store ignores injected keys and starts from the built-in defaults.
A release-policy launch ignores injected counter state lacking the provenance marker, falling back to the four default starter counters.
Once the app stamps provenance, a release-policy AppSettings launch trusts the store's own settings again.
Under the release policy, a real user's own persisted data survives: once the app persists (stamping the marker), a reload trusts it.
reset() and undoReset() are not count-change events — they stay silent.
Resetting a counter already at zero still enters undo mode; undoing restores zero.
Reset captures the pre-reset value and enters undo mode.
Reset seals the current run and opens a new empty run; the count zeroes.
Reset zeroes the active counter without touching the others.
A hand-authored history seed (JSON object keyed by counter id, epoch-millis times) loads with correct deltas and relative offsets.
The seed read coerces a string-injected value via the store's int coercion.
A model seeded with the resetUndo key enters undo mode on launch when the active counter is at zero (the static-scenario seed path).
The seed is rejected when the active counter is not at zero — a stale leftover key must not falsely activate UNDO RESET.
A seeded subset (no deletedDefaultIds) has no blank slots.
Swiping forward within the list advances selection by one and does not grow it.
Swiping forward PAST the last counter grows the list: it appends a fresh blank slot and selects it instead of wrapping back to the first.
selectPrevious within the list moves back by one.
selectPrevious wraps around from the first counter to the last, never growing.
With negatives disallowed, a step that would overshoot below zero clamps to zero.
A counter with allowNegative == false clamps at zero instead of going negative.
Subtracting also clears the pending undo.

With the default allowNegative == true, subtracting from zero goes negative.
Subtracting honors the step symmetrically when negatives are allowed.
The no-op clamp (negatives disallowed, already at zero) fires no feedback.
Subtract records the actual (negative) applied delta.

The default (debug) trust policy still adopts injected state.
undoReset restores the count AND pops the empty run reset opened.
undoReset restores the captured value and exits undo mode.

Saving with null overrides clears any previously pinned values.

Each isolated channel maps to the expected fraction of 255.
The lime accent decomposes into its three channels.
Pure black and white sit at the ends of the 0..1 range.

Every qualitatively-distinct feel gates the same way: non-OFF, so each fires the haptic emitter once carrying its own choice.

Both off → nothing fires.
Both non-off → both emitters fire once with their respective choices.

An increment-haptic override alone is enough to open the section.
A counter left on pure app-wide defaults pins nothing, so the section stays collapsed.
The no-op default implementation never touches its arguments — a smoke check that calling it with any options is safe and silent.

A sound override alone is enough to open the section.

The closing direction for the per-counter panel.

Spot-checks a specific sound-to-tone mapping is stable.
